newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares fall sharply on Yeltsin news.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares fall sharply on Yeltsin news.

text.p: Prices of leading Russian shares fell sharply on Thursday after news President Boris Yeltsin had agreed to undergo a heart operation, dealers said.
"The thing's gone down, everybody is selling, and it's not looking good," said Nick Mokhoff, head of equities trading at Alliance-Menatep, adding that shares were likely to fall further on Friday.
Yeltsin's spokesman confirmed the 65-year-old Kremlin leader had agreed to undergo heart surgery later this month.

"I don't see good things for the next two or three days," said Victor Pitaleff of Renaissance Capital. "There will be a lot of speculation as to how serious the operation will be. After the presidential election the market fell 20 or 30 percent on nothing."

At 1400 GMT UES was traded at $0.0815 compared with $0.0828 before the news and Wednesday's closing $0.083. Mosenergo, regarded as a bellwether of the market, was at $0.970 after $0.995 and Wednesday's closing $1.010. LUKoil was at $9.60 after $9.84 and Wednesday's $9.85.
Russian shares rose sharply on prospects of Yeltsin's victory, but fell back heavily after he won the July 3 run-off when hoped-for new Western investment did not materialise.
But in recent weeks prices have been edging up again.
Western investors have said the health of the Russian leader, who has rarely been seen in public since late June, is a major damper on prices.
But traders said the operation could work to the market's advantage by clearing up uncertainty about Yeltsin's health.
"A night's reflection should be enough for most people in this market to see it is not a serious negative," said Troika-Dialog trader Terry Olin.
"What we're seeing now is not happening on any volume. This should not carry past tomorrow morning."
